title: BAGMAN ExternalReference
description: Canonical `ExternalReference` (PID §10). Represents an external, provider-native identifier separately from BAGMAN's own canonical identities, e.g. 'BAGMAN evidence EV-... corresponds to Microsoft Graph message AAMk...' without contaminating BAGMAN's internal identity model. Placement note: this schema lives under `contracts/source/` rather than a dedicated `contracts/external_reference/` folder — the PID's suggested layout (§18) does not list a separate folder for ExternalReference, and §9/§10 introduce ExternalReference immediately after, and in the same conceptual family as, Source; see `contracts/README.md` for the full placement rationale. COMPOSITE UNIQUENESS RULE (PID §10, §34): `external_id` is a raw provider-native identifier and is NEVER assumed globally unique on its own. Uniqueness is scoped to the tuple (`provider`, `source_id`, `resource_type`, `external_id`) taken together. The same `external_id` value may legitimately reappear under a different provider, source, or resource type without collision. Idempotent re-observation of the same (`provider`, `source_id`, `resource_type`, `external_id`) tuple must not blindly produce duplicate canonical records unless the domain explicitly allows separate observations (PID §34) — enforced at the domain/repository layer, not by this schema alone.

external_reference_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this external-reference record itself.

provider.description: The external provider/system that issued `external_id`, e.g. `MICROSOFT_GRAPH`, `XERO`, `STARLING`. Part of the composite uniqueness scope (see top-level description).

resource_type.description: The kind of external resource being referenced, e.g. `EMAIL_MESSAGE`, `BANK_TRANSACTION`, `INVOICE`. Part of the composite uniqueness scope (see top-level description).

external_id.description: The raw, provider-native identifier as issued by the external system, e.g. a Microsoft Graph message ID. This value is NEVER assumed globally unique on its own — see the composite uniqueness rule in this schema's top-level description. Part of the composite uniqueness scope.

canonical_object_type.description: The BAGMAN-internal canonical object type that this external reference maps to, e.g. `EvidenceItem`.

canonical_object_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier of the internal object (of type `canonical_object_type`) that this external reference maps to.

source_id.description: Canonical identifier of the `Source` this external reference was observed through. Part of the composite uniqueness scope (see top-level description).

first_observed_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this external reference was first observed by BAGMAN.

metadata.description: Free-form, genuinely open metadata about this external reference.
